Types of Dermal Fillers Gallery Benefits Candidates Preparation Procedure Recovery Results Cost FAQs Consultation Contours in All the Right Places What Are Dermal Fillers? Dermal fillers are injectable gels used to replace or enhance soft tissue volume beneath the skin . Most are made from hyaluronic acid (HA), a substance your body already produces to keep skin hydrated and resilient. As we age, natural HA production slows, collagen fibers loosen, and fat pads shift, creating shadows and hollows where the face once had gentle fullness. By strategically placing filler in precise layers, we can smooth folds, restore youthful curves, and define structural points like the cheekbones or jawline. At our Wellesley-area clinic, we offer a variety of FDA-approved fillers, each with its own texture, density, and longevity, allowing us to customize every treatment. Some fillers are designed to move with your expressions for natural animation , while others hold their shape for long-lasting structural support. Choosing the Right Molecule Types of Dermal Fillers Not all fillers serve the same purpose. The viscosity of the gel determines where it belongs in the face. Hyaluronic Acid (HA) Fillers: This category includes the JuvÃ©dermÂ® and RestylaneÂ® families. They are versatile, reversible, and range from thin, hydrating gels for vertical lip lines to robust formulas for cheek lifting. Biostimulatory Fillers: Products like RadiesseÂ® or SculptraÂ® work differently. Instead of just providing immediate volume, they act as a scaffold that encourages your body to produce its own new collagen over several months. Specialized Lip Fillers: These are engineered for the high-mobility environment of the mouth, ensuring the lips look soft and natural whether you are speaking, smiling, or at rest. Precision Mapping What Can Dermal Fillers Address? The scope of filler application has expanded far beyond the "filling of lines." We use these injectables to address structural concerns across the entire face: Midface Restoration : Rebuilding cheek volume to lift the lower face and soften the appearance of the nasolabial folds. Perioral Refinement : Blurring the "smokerâs lines" around the mouth and restoring lost definition to the lip border. Jawline and Chin Contouring : Sharpening the profile and creating a distinct separation between the face and neck. Tear Trough Correction : Filling the hollows under the eyes to reduce the appearance of persistent tiredness. Temple Rejuvenation : Softening the "hollowing" at the temples that can create a skeletal look. Scar Revision : Improving the texture and depth of certain indented or atrophic scars. Your consultation will include a review of your medical history and any conditions that could affect safety or outcome. Not Every Face Needs the Same Map What Can Fillers Address? The range of what fillers can address is broad. In the midface, they can restore cheek volume and smooth the transition from under-eye to cheek . Around the mouth, they soften folds and lines without adding bulk. In the lips, they add fullness, refine shape, and blur vertical lines . Along the jaw or chin, fillers can define edges or balance the profile. Even the temples â an often-overlooked area â can benefit from a touch of volume, lending a more rested appearance. What Weâll Talk About First Dermal Fillers Consultation and Preparation Your dermal filler treatment starts with a thorough conversation. Weâll ask about your aesthetic priorities, daily lifestyle, and whether youâve had filler before. Preparation is minimal but important. To reduce bruising risk, we usually recommend avoiding aspirin, ibuprofen, certain herbal supplements, and alcohol for a few days before your appointment. If youâre prone to swelling, you may benefit from adding arnica or bromelain into your pre-treatment routine. We also ask that you arrive with clean, product-free skin so treatment can begin promptly. Weâll check progress throughout the session, making micro-adjustments until everything looks balanced. Dermal Filler injections typically take 30 to 45 minutes , though more complex treatments may run slightly longer. Youâll be able to return to most regular activities right away, though weâll review a few short-term restrictions to protect your results. Your Skinâs Favorite Weekend Dermal Filler Recovery and Aftercare Itâs common to have mild swelling or pinpoint redness at injection sites for a day or two. Small bruises may occasionally appear, especially in more delicate areas like the lips, but they usually fade quickly. Weâll give you personalized aftercare instructions, typically avoiding intense exercise, alcohol, and direct heat (like saunas) for 24 hours. Gentle icing can help reduce swelling, and makeup can usually be applied the next day if needed. Youâll see a difference before you leave the office, though final results look even better once swelling subsides. Longevity depends on the filler type, placement, and your own metabolism. Softer fillers used in lips may last 6 to 9 months , while firmer structural fillers in the cheeks or jawline can last 12 to 24 months.
